Definition: total slow-wave sleep (SWS) time as a percentage of the 24-hour day
Note: printed footnote e: total SWS is LESS than left-hemisphere SWS plus right-hemisphere SWS, because cetaceans have unihemispheric SWS and episodes of bilateral sleep with EEG asymmetry - the two hemisphere columns overlap and must never be summed

Definition: SWS recorded in the LEFT cerebral hemisphere, as a percentage of the 24-hour day
Note: per-hemisphere amounts differ between individuals within a 24 h period

Definition: SWS recorded in the RIGHT cerebral hemisphere, as a percentage of the 24-hour day
Source Note: printed Table 2 row 'SWS in right hemisphere'

Definition: low-amplitude unihemispheric slow-wave sleep (USWS) as a percentage of total sleep time (TST)
Note: USWS = a state in which slow-wave EEG is recorded in one hemisphere (alternately left or right) while EEG desynchronization is recorded simultaneously in the other (Mukhametov's definition). TST = total sleep time. This and the four rows below are the composition of SWS and sum to about 100% of TST
Source Note: printed Table 2 row 'Low amplitude USWS' under the heading 'Composition of SWS (% of TST)'; USWS definition quoted in sec. 2.3, p. 1453

Definition: high-amplitude USWS as a percentage of total sleep time
Note: low- plus high-amplitude USWS is what the project's USWS_pctTST term sums; across these species USWS is 70-90% of total sleep time
Source Note: printed Table 2 row 'High amplitude USWS'; 70-90% figure in the text, p. 1456

Definition: asymmetrical (but bilateral) SWS as a percentage of total sleep time - high-voltage slow waves in one hemisphere with low-voltage slow waves in the other
Note: distinct from USWS: both hemispheres show slow waves, at different amplitudes. Together with bilateral SWS this occupies the remaining 10-30% of total sleep time
Source Note: printed Table 2 row 'Asymmetrical SWS'; description in the text, p. 1456

Definition: low-amplitude bilateral SWS as a percentage of total sleep time
Source Note: printed Table 2 row 'Low amplitude bilateral SWS'

Definition: high-amplitude bilateral SWS as a percentage of total sleep time
Note: essentially absent: 0.0 in three species and 0.2 in the beluga
Source Note: printed Table 2 row 'High amplitude bilateral SWS'

Definition: project standardized term: total slow-wave sleep as a per cent of the 24-hour day
Note: project standardized term; per cent of 24 h, NOT per cent of total sleep time - do not pool with percent-of-sleep terms

Definition: project standardized term: unihemispheric slow-wave sleep as a per cent of total sleep time, computed as low-amplitude USWS + high-amplitude USWS
Note: project standardized term; a derived sum of two printed rows, not a printed value. Distinct construct from the free-text USWS field in Capellini_etal_2008_sleep-data - never pool the two

Definition: chronic EEG recording from both cerebral hemispheres in captive cetaceans using the tethered wire/harness technique, scored for unihemispheric versus bilateral slow-wave sleep
Note: no REM column exists: the paper argues cetaceans show a negligible amount or complete absence of classical REM sleep, and that absence is itself the finding. Animals were in shallow pools or movement-restricted; conditions differ between the four columns
